description:
FILED s477 (Fable, 2026-09-07) from the s473d review probes.  PRE-EXISTING: reproduces identically on main 37b7e83b and on the s473d tree (0c90e681), so it is NOT caused by #1248(c)'s storage change (simple vector -> adjustable vector without fill pointer); it is the aliasing path, not the storage.

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, default AND PCL_OPT=none):
  my @a = (1..3); Internals::SvREADONLY(@a, 1);
  for my $e (@a) { $e *= 2 }  print "foreach-ro: @a\n";   # perl: 2 4 6      PCL: 1 2 3
  $_ *= 10 for @a;            print "postfix-ro: @a\n";   # perl: 20 40 60   PCL: 1 2 3
  $a[0] = 99;                 print "elem-ro: @a\n";      # perl: 99 40 60   PCL: 99 2 3   (element write lands)
  map { $_++ } @a;            print "map-ro: @a\n";       # perl: 100 41 61  PCL: 100 3 4  (map alias write lands)
  my @b = (1..3); for my $e (@b) { $e *= 2 }  print "@b\n";  # 2 4 6 on both (writable array: foreach alias works)

The discriminating fact: `map`'s alias write lands but `foreach`'s does not, so the two loops alias a read-only array's elements through DIFFERENT mechanisms and the foreach one (the foreach-raw / boxed-aggregates alias path, `p-foreach` and its raw-element write-back) tests something a read-only storage fails -- most likely the same "is this an array" / "is it writable" conflation #1248(c) found at sixteen scalar-collapse sites (ir-spec section 2.3's two-question table): the write-back probably asks ARRAY-HAS-FILL-POINTER-P (writability of the SIZE) where it means "may I store into the slot" (always yes: perl's read-only AV has writable elements).  PCL_OPT=none gives the same answer, so it is not only the Kind-A foreach-raw emission.

Fix shape (rule 11): find the ONE write-back predicate foreach's alias uses, make it ask the element-store question (never the size question), guard rows in Pl/t/numeric-repr-01.t's read-only section or a readonly-array guard file (both loops + map + the writable control), inverse-verified.  Bars: runtime-only -> gate + full sweep + companion op/array.t; ir-conform.  A fix must NOT relax the size-change fatals (push/pop/splice/aassign/$#a still die).
subject: A foreach ALIAS write to an element of a READ-ONLY array does not land: `for my $e (@a) { $e *= 2 }` and `$_ *= 10 for @a` leave @a unchanged after Internals::SvREADONLY(@a,1); perl writes the elements (only the SIZE is frozen); `$a[0] = 99` and `map { $_++ } @a` DO land
